# Roamstay company context

Maintained by Leila, Product Operations Lead. Last reviewed on 2026-09-18.

Roamstay is a hotel booking marketplace. Guests search and book stays at hotels, guesthouses and serviced apartments, and partners list and run their properties on it. About 18,000 properties are live, across Europe and the United States.

## Product and surfaces

Roamstay has three surfaces. Each has its own owners and its own release rhythm.

| Surface | Used by | Platforms | Covers |
|---------|---------|-----------|--------|
| Guest app | Guests | iOS, Android, web | Search, property page, checkout, trips, account, chat with Guest Support |
| Partner Hub | Partners | Web, built for desktop | Property profile, rooms, rates and availability, policies, city tax, payouts, bookings list, guest reviews |
| Back office | Ops agents, Guest Support | Web, staff only | Booking lookup, refunds and rebooking, partner verification, go-live review, payout holds |

When a ticket says Guest app without a platform, it means iOS, Android and web together. The web version uses the same services as the apps, but it is built and released on its own.

Partner Hub is where a partner changes what guests see. A price, a photo, a cancellation policy or a city tax rule saved there reaches the Guest app through `partner-service` within 5 minutes.

Back office is invisible to guests and partners. Every refund, rebooking or payout hold made there is logged against the agent who made it.

## Personas and roles

| Persona | Works in | What they do |
|---------|----------|--------------|
| Guest | Guest app | Searches, books and manages stays. Can book signed in or with an email address only |
| Partner | Partner Hub | Runs one or more properties. Partner Hub users are Owner, Manager or Front desk, and only an Owner can change payout details |
| Ops agent | Back office | Roamstay staff who verify new partners, set up and check properties before go-live and handle partner escalations |
| Guest Support agent | Back office and the support desk tool | Answers guest chats and emails in six languages and escalates product defects to the owning squad as a ticket |

Guest Support is its own team inside Operations, next to the Ops agents. A defect reaches a squad as a Guest Support ticket with a priority of Low, Medium, High or Urgent, set by the Tier 2 agent who escalates it.

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| Stay | One booking's dates at one property, counted in nights. Check-in on a Monday and check-out on a Thursday is 3 nights |
| Property | A hotel, guesthouse or apartment building listed by a partner, identified by a numeric property ID |
| Room type | A kind of room at a property, such as Double room or Family suite, with a maximum occupancy |
| Rate plan | A price for a room type with its own cancellation policy and payment option. One room type often has two or three |
| Free cancellation | A rate plan policy that refunds the guest in full if they cancel before a deadline the partner sets |
| Non-refundable | A rate plan policy with no refund after booking, usually priced lower |
| City tax | A local tax the partner enters in Partner Hub, per adult per night or per stay. It shows as its own `City tax` line in the price breakdown and is part of the total |
| Pay now | The guest pays the full total at booking, and the payment provider charges the card |
| Pay at property | The guest's card is stored as a guarantee and the guest pays the property on arrival |
| Booking reference | `RS-` followed by six letters and digits. It is on the confirmation screen, in every email and in Back office |
| `payment_pending` | The booking state between Pay now and the payment provider's confirmation |
| Go-live | The moment a new property becomes bookable in the Guest app |
| Payout | Money Roamstay sends a partner for completed stays, after commission |

## Services and integrations

| Service | Owner squad | Responsibility |
|---------|-------------|----------------|
| `search-service` | Search | Availability search, ranking, filters and paging, at `25 results` per page |
| `booking-service` | Booking | Creates bookings, owns booking states and references, sends confirmation emails |
| `payments-service` | Payments | Card payments, refunds and payouts with the payment provider, and the webhooks it sends back |
| `partner-service` | Partner | Properties, room types, rate plans, policies, city tax rules and partner users |
| `events-collector` | Data | Receives analytics events from the apps, the web and the services |

Third parties appear by role in tickets and docs, never by name:

- The payment provider takes card payments for Pay now, stores cards for Pay at property and sends partner payouts. Only `payments-service` talks to it, and it reports payment results back by webhook
- The map provider serves map tiles and geocoding for search and the property page
- The email delivery provider sends booking confirmations for `booking-service` and partner emails for `partner-service`
- A channel manager is a partner's own tool for pushing rates and availability to several booking sites at once. It connects to `partner-service` through the partner API
- The identity verification provider checks the identity documents of property owners during partner verification

## Teams and discipline codes

Product and engineering work in six squads: Search, Booking, Payments, Partner, Ops Tools and Data. A Design System group works across all of them. Each squad has a product manager, a product designer and engineers for the surfaces it owns.

| Code | Discipline | Typical work |
|------|------------|--------------|
| `FE` | Front end | Guest app screens on iOS, Android and web, Partner Hub screens |
| `BE` | Back end | Services, APIs, scheduled jobs and webhooks |
| `BO` | Back office | Back office tools and internal flows for Ops agents and Guest Support |
| `FS` | Full stack | One change across a screen and its service, when splitting it would ship half a feature |
| `DATA` | Data and tracking | Tracking events, the tracking plan, dashboards |
| `DS` | Design system | Shared components, tokens and icons |

Task and bug titles follow `{Discipline} - {Surface} - {Feature code} - {Title}`. The surface is Guest app, Partner Hub or Back office, and the feature code comes from the next section. Two titles from the current backlog: `FE - Partner Hub - PHUB - Bulk rate editor` and `BO - Back office - OPS - Refund reason codes`.

Story and epic titles carry no discipline code. A story title reads `{Persona or surface} - {Area} - {Feature}`, as in `Guest - Trips - Add a stay to the calendar`, and an epic title reads `Epic - {Persona or surface} - {Area}`.

## Feature codes

| Code | Area | Owner squad |
|------|------|-------------|
| `SRCH` | Search form, date picker, results list, filters, sort, map | Search |
| `PROP` | Property page, photos, room list, guest reviews | Search |
| `BOOK` | Checkout, booking states, confirmation screen, trips, cancellation | Booking |
| `PAY` | Pay now, Pay at property, refunds, payouts, payment webhooks | Payments |
| `PHUB` | Partner Hub rates, availability, policies, city tax, bookings list | Partner |
| `ONB` | Partner sign-up, verification and go-live | Partner |
| `TRK` | Analytics events and the tracking plan | Data |
| `OPS` | Back office tools for Ops agents and Guest Support | Ops Tools |

A piece of work takes the code of the area it changes, whichever squad picks it up. A city tax change on the checkout screen is `BOOK`, and the setup screen for the same rule in Partner Hub is `PHUB`.

## Platforms and app versions

| Platform | Current version | Released | Minimum OS |
|----------|-----------------|----------|------------|
| iOS | `8.12.0` | `2026-09-16` | iOS 16 |
| Android | `8.12.1` | `2026-09-16` | Android 9 |
| Web | Continuous deploys | Several times a day | Last two major versions of the main browsers |

The apps ship on a two-week release train. The branch is cut on a Monday and the builds go to the stores on the Wednesday after. The previous train was 8.11.2 on both platforms, released on 2026-09-02.

Android went out as 8.12.1 because the 8.12.0 build was turned back by the store over a permissions text, so the two apps carry different numbers for the same train. Android rolls out in stages over 5 days, iOS to everyone on release day.

Apps below 8.6.0 show a forced update screen. Partner Hub and Back office are web only and deploy continuously, like the web version of the Guest app.

## Currencies and locales

Roamstay supports five currencies: `EUR`, `GBP`, `USD`, `CHF` and `SEK`. A partner sets one currency per property in Partner Hub, and the Guest app shows and charges prices in that currency. There is no currency conversion.

Services and events carry money as an integer in minor units. The apps format it for the guest's locale, so the same amount shows as €1,240.50 in `en-GB` and as 1.240,50 € in `de-DE`.

| Locale | Language | Notes |
|--------|----------|-------|
| `en-GB` | English | Default, and the fallback for any missing string |
| `en-US` | English | US spelling, week starts on Sunday |
| `de-DE` | German | Strings run about 30% longer than English, check button widths |
| `fr-FR` | French | Space before the currency sign in prices |
| `es-ES` | Spanish | Space before the currency sign in prices |
| `it-IT` | Italian | Space before the currency sign in prices |
| `nl-NL` | Dutch | Currency sign before the amount, with a space |

Every locale except `en-US` starts the week on Monday. The apps follow the device locale for dates and prices, and the web follows the browser locale. Partner Hub is available in the same seven locales.

## Key flows

### Search

The guest enters a destination, check-in and check-out dates, guests and rooms. A stay runs from 1 night to `30 nights` and check-in can be at most `365 days` ahead. One search covers up to `8 rooms`. `search-service` returns `25 results` per page, sorted by Recommended. The apps load the next page on scroll. The filter sheet holds two filters today, Price and Star rating.

### Property page

The property page shows photos, room types and, for each room type, its rate plans with their cancellation policy and payment option. A partner can set a minimum stay for the property, which the date picker applies on this page.

### Checkout and payment

The guest enters their details and picks a rate plan's payment option. The price breakdown lists the room price per night and the total, with a `City tax` line between them when the property charges it.

With `Pay now`, the payment provider charges the full total, city tax included. The booking waits in `payment_pending` until the payment provider confirms by webhook, then moves to confirmed. A booking still in `payment_pending` after `30 minutes` expires and its room goes back on sale.

With `Pay at property`, the card is stored as a guarantee and the booking confirms at once. The guest pays the property on arrival, city tax included.

### Confirmation and trips

The confirmation screen shows the booking reference, dates, guests and the total. `booking-service` sends the confirmation email at the same moment. The stay then lives under Trips, where the guest can view it, change dates or cancel.

### Cancellation

Before the free cancellation deadline, the guest cancels under Trips and the refund goes back to the card through the payment provider. After the deadline, or on a non-refundable rate plan, the guest contacts Guest Support.

### Partner onboarding today

A partner signs up with a short form on the web. An Ops agent then sets up the property in Back office from the details the partner sends by email. The same agent checks identity and payout details and makes the property live.

## Known constraints

- A stay is at most `30 nights`, and check-in is at most `365 days` ahead
- One booking holds at most `8 rooms`
- A booking in `payment_pending` expires after `30 minutes`
- Prices show and charge in the property's currency, with no conversion
- Roamstay has no loyalty or points scheme. Guests earn no points, and there are no member tiers or member-only prices
- Guests who book with an email address only cannot save a card
- Partner Hub has no mobile app, and its screens are designed for desktop widths
- Back office needs a staff account and is never exposed to partners
- Guest Support covers 07:00 to 23:00 CET, seven days a week

## Analytics conventions

- Event names follow `object_action` in snake_case, with the action in the past tense
- A search filter the guest turns on fires `filter_applied`, with `filter_name` saying which filter
- Every client event carries `app_version`, `session_id`, `platform` and `locale`
- Server events carry the `session_id` of the request that caused them, so client and server events join on it
- Every event carries `source`, which is `client` or `server`
- Money travels as an integer in minor units, in a property whose name ends in `_minor`, with a `currency` property beside it. €129.50 is sent as `12950`
- Events go to `events-collector`, which accepts events from the apps, the web and the services
- The Data team owns the tracking plan. Each event has a row with its trigger, its properties and a status, and a squad builds an event from its row

# Product Owner Hub

One public skill identity over three workflow packets and one transport packet. This hub holds no packet-local logic. It routes by `workflowMode` through `mode-registry.json`, uses `hub-router.json` for router policy, signals and outcomes, and hands stage two to the root `ROUTER.md`, which maps the request's intent to the packet's leaves.

**Version authority.** This file's `version` frontmatter is the hub's release version and matches the newest entry under `changelog/`. `description.json`, `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` carry the same value. `ROUTER.md` keeps its own document version, and each packet keeps its own release line.

---

## 1. WHEN TO USE

Use this skill for Barter backlog and documentation work, for diagrams drawn on FigJam boards, and for the ClickUp and Figma operations those artifacts travel through.

| Mode | Kind | Use it for | Packet |
|------|------|------------|--------|
| **sk-product-owner** | workflow | Every task, bug, Story, Epic, Doc and clarification request. The default | [`sk-product-owner/`](sk-product-owner/SKILL.md) |
| **sk-create-figjam** | workflow | A diagram drawn on a FigJam board, from a user flow to a sequence, state, ER or gantt chart: `$flow`, `$figjam` or FigJam output wording with no Product Owner artifact named | [`sk-create-figjam/`](sk-create-figjam/SKILL.md) |
| **mcp-click-up** | workflow | A request that opens with a `cupt` or ClickUp MCP operation, or names one and no Product Owner artifact. Vendored | [`mcp-click-up/`](mcp-click-up/SKILL.md) |
| **mcp-figma** | transport | A request that opens with a `figma-ds-cli` operation, or names one and no Product Owner artifact. Vendored, read-only in this workspace | [`mcp-figma/`](mcp-figma/SKILL.md) |

### When NOT to Use

- Production code or a live fix. The Product Owner packet reframes the request or declines it
- Editing a vendored packet. A change to `mcp-click-up/` or `mcp-figma/` goes upstream through `scripts/vendor-sync.py push`

---

## 2. SMART ROUTING

Routing is registry-driven in two stages. Stage one picks the mode here, from `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json`. Stage two is the root [`ROUTER.md`](ROUTER.md), which maps the request's intent to the exact packet-local leaves that mode loads, and the packet's own `SKILL.md` Section 2 routes inside the packet. The hub never emits leaf paths, and `ROUTER.md` never re-decides the mode.

> **Compiled routing (default-on, flag-gated, additive).** Resolve the mode via the compiled router contract first:
> ```bash
> node .skilled/bin/compiled-route.cjs --hub product-owner --prompt "<task>"
> ```
> Follow the returned decision: `route` (use its `targets`), `clarify` or `defer` (disambiguate) or `reject` (refuse). On a `{"servingAuthority":"legacy"}` sentinel or any error, use the routing below. The front door self-gates on serving-authority. Compiled routing is the default for `product-owner`. Set `SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=0`, the explicit kill-switch, to force legacy routing fleet-wide.

`product-owner` ships without a compiled activation manifest, so the directive above returns the legacy sentinel and the stage one rules below route every request. A Product Owner clone that has no `.skilled/bin/` gets an error from the same command and takes the same path.

### Stage One Rules

Stage one follows the ordered rules in [`hub-router.json`](hub-router.json) `routerPolicy.stageOneOrder`. The first matching rule wins. Packet commands run first, then an artifact request, then an opening packet signal, a default artifact word, one non-negated packet signal, and the default mode.

Examples: `cupt list my open tasks` stays in `mcp-click-up` because `tasks` is data, while `figma-ds-cli fj nodes` opens in `mcp-figma`. `figma-ds-cli fj nodes and write a task for the spacing` and `figjam the checkout flow, then write a story` start in `sk-product-owner` because each asks for an artifact. The bare words "figma" and "clickup" remain subjects, and a negated signal such as "do not use figma-ds-cli" starts no packet. A `figma.com/board` link is a FigJam signal, because that address is a FigJam file, while a `figma.com/design` link is not. A full stop ends a clause only before a space, so the dots inside a link stay in the clause that carries it.

A Flow request that stage one keeps in the Product Owner packet follows the single-route handoff contract in [`sk-product-owner/SKILL.md`](sk-product-owner/SKILL.md) Section 2. A command conflict such as `$task $flow` follows that packet's Interactive route.


### Outcomes

- `single`: one packet's commands or signals route to that one mode
- `orderedBundle`: never formed here. Signals of two packets start in the default mode, whose Interactive Mode asks which comes first. A FigJam second output beside an artifact is the exception, because it forms an ordered pair in stage two with the artifact first, while two artifacts still ask
- `defer`: a request with no packet command or signal starts in the default mode, and one it cannot route there gets one clarifying question

`benchmark/hub-routing-cases.json` holds the hub gold rows, and `benchmark/gates/check_hub.py` replays them against these rules and checks that the hub files, the registry, the router and the packets agree.

---

## 3. HOW IT WORKS

### Layout

```text
Product Owner/            the repository root is the hub
  SKILL.md                 this routing hub
  ROUTER.md                stage two: intent to packet-local leaves
  mode-registry.json       the four modes and the discriminator
  hub-router.json          router policy, signals and vocabulary classes
  description.json         hub advisor descriptor
  graph-metadata.json      the ONE advisor identity for the whole hub
  leaf-manifest.json       generated (workflowMode, leaf) pairs
  changelog/  manual-testing-playbook/  benchmark/
  sk-product-owner/        workflow: tasks, bugs, Stories, Epics, docs
  sk-create-figjam/        workflow: FigJam diagrams
  mcp-click-up/            workflow: vendored ClickUp transport
  mcp-figma/               transport: vendored Figma Desktop bridge
  mcp-code-mode/           the vendored Code Mode server, a repository file and no packet
  AGENTS.md  SYNC.md  vendor.json  opencode.json  LICENSE  Favicon.jpg
  specs/  export/  claude project/  scripts/
                           repository files, declared in the repo-root-hub extension
```

`mcp-code-mode/` carries its own `leaf-manifest.json` because it is the Code Mode server this repository ships beside the packets, not a workflow packet, so the rule against a leaf manifest inside a packet does not reach it. The hub shares the repository root with the bootstrap `AGENTS.md`, the Claude Project package, the spec packets, the exports, the system gates in `benchmark/` and the tooling in `scripts/`. `mode-registry.json` lists those repository entries in its `repo-root-hub` extension, so the skilled checkers skip them and read the hub id from the folder name in kebab case. Each vendored packet is a byte-identical copy of a shared skill: `vendor.json` records its upstream and `scripts/vendor-sync.py` keeps it in step, so its routing stays in its own `SKILL.md`. Only this hub carries a `graph-metadata.json`, so the advisor discovers one `product-owner` identity.

---

## 4. RULES

### ALWAYS

- **ALWAYS** read `AGENTS.md` first when it is not already loaded, as when a runtime opens this skill directly, because it holds the export protocol and the identity handoff
- **ALWAYS** resolve a packet through `mode-registry.json`, then read `ROUTER.md` and the packet's `SKILL.md`
- **ALWAYS** keep each workflow packet's routing in its `SKILL.md` Section 2 and its leaf map in the root `ROUTER.md`
- **ALWAYS** regenerate `leaf-manifest.json` with the sk-create-skill generator after a packet gains or loses a reference or asset

### NEVER

- **NEVER** add a `ROUTER.md`, `graph-metadata.json` or leaf-manifest file inside a packet
- **NEVER** edit `mcp-figma/` or `mcp-click-up/` without moving the change through `scripts/vendor-sync.py push`
- **NEVER** put packet logic in this hub

### ESCALATE IF

- A new kind of Product Owner work needs its own packet. Extend `mode-registry.json`, `hub-router.json` and `ROUTER.md` together and open the packet
- A request names two packets' signals and the Product Owner packet cannot tell which comes first

# Roamstay company context

Maintained by Leila, Product Operations Lead. Last reviewed on 2026-09-18.

Roamstay is a hotel booking marketplace. Guests search and book stays at hotels, guesthouses and serviced apartments, and partners list and run their properties on it. About 18,000 properties are live, across Europe and the United States.

## Product and surfaces

Roamstay has three surfaces. Each has its own owners and its own release rhythm.

| Surface | Used by | Platforms | Covers |
|---------|---------|-----------|--------|
| Guest app | Guests | iOS, Android, web | Search, property page, checkout, trips, account, chat with Guest Support |
| Partner Hub | Partners | Web, built for desktop | Property profile, rooms, rates and availability, policies, city tax, payouts, bookings list, guest reviews |
| Back office | Ops agents, Guest Support | Web, staff only | Booking lookup, refunds and rebooking, partner verification, go-live review, payout holds |

When a ticket says Guest app without a platform, it means iOS, Android and web together. The web version uses the same services as the apps, but it is built and released on its own.

Partner Hub is where a partner changes what guests see. A price, a photo, a cancellation policy or a city tax rule saved there reaches the Guest app through `partner-service` within 5 minutes.

Back office is invisible to guests and partners. Every refund, rebooking or payout hold made there is logged against the agent who made it.

## Personas and roles

| Persona | Works in | What they do |
|---------|----------|--------------|
| Guest | Guest app | Searches, books and manages stays. Can book signed in or with an email address only |
| Partner | Partner Hub | Runs one or more properties. Partner Hub users are Owner, Manager or Front desk, and only an Owner can change payout details |
| Ops agent | Back office | Roamstay staff who verify new partners, set up and check properties before go-live and handle partner escalations |
| Guest Support agent | Back office and the support desk tool | Answers guest chats and emails in six languages and escalates product defects to the owning squad as a ticket |

Guest Support is its own team inside Operations, next to the Ops agents. A defect reaches a squad as a Guest Support ticket with a priority of Low, Medium, High or Urgent, set by the Tier 2 agent who escalates it.

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| Stay | One booking's dates at one property, counted in nights. Check-in on a Monday and check-out on a Thursday is 3 nights |
| Property | A hotel, guesthouse or apartment building listed by a partner, identified by a numeric property ID |
| Room type | A kind of room at a property, such as Double room or Family suite, with a maximum occupancy |
| Rate plan | A price for a room type with its own cancellation policy and payment option. One room type often has two or three |
| Free cancellation | A rate plan policy that refunds the guest in full if they cancel before a deadline the partner sets |
| Non-refundable | A rate plan policy with no refund after booking, usually priced lower |
| City tax | A local tax the partner enters in Partner Hub, per adult per night or per stay. It shows as its own `City tax` line in the price breakdown and is part of the total |
| Pay now | The guest pays the full total at booking, and the payment provider charges the card |
| Pay at property | The guest's card is stored as a guarantee and the guest pays the property on arrival |
| Booking reference | `RS-` followed by six letters and digits. It is on the confirmation screen, in every email and in Back office |
| `payment_pending` | The booking state between Pay now and the payment provider's confirmation |
| Go-live | The moment a new property becomes bookable in the Guest app |
| Payout | Money Roamstay sends a partner for completed stays, after commission |

## Services and integrations

| Service | Owner squad | Responsibility |
|---------|-------------|----------------|
| `search-service` | Search | Availability search, ranking, filters and paging, at `25 results` per page |
| `booking-service` | Booking | Creates bookings, owns booking states and references, sends confirmation emails |
| `payments-service` | Payments | Card payments, refunds and payouts with the payment provider, and the webhooks it sends back |
| `partner-service` | Partner | Properties, room types, rate plans, policies, city tax rules and partner users |
| `events-collector` | Data | Receives analytics events from the apps, the web and the services |

Third parties appear by role in tickets and docs, never by name:

- The payment provider takes card payments for Pay now, stores cards for Pay at property and sends partner payouts. Only `payments-service` talks to it, and it reports payment results back by webhook
- The map provider serves map tiles and geocoding for search and the property page
- The email delivery provider sends booking confirmations for `booking-service` and partner emails for `partner-service`
- A channel manager is a partner's own tool for pushing rates and availability to several booking sites at once. It connects to `partner-service` through the partner API
- The identity verification provider checks the identity documents of property owners during partner verification

Product and engineering work in six squads: Search, Booking, Payments, Partner, Ops Tools and Data. A Design System group works across all of them. Each squad has a product manager, a product designer and engineers for the surfaces it owns.

|------|------------|--------------|
| `FE` | Front end | Guest app screens on iOS, Android and web, Partner Hub screens |
| `BE` | Back end | Services, APIs, scheduled jobs and webhooks |
| `BO` | Back office | Back office tools and internal flows for Ops agents and Guest Support |
| `FS` | Full stack | One change across a screen and its service, when splitting it would ship half a feature |
| `DATA` | Data and tracking | Tracking events, the tracking plan, dashboards |
| `DS` | Design system | Shared components, tokens and icons |

Task and bug titles follow `{Discipline} - {Surface} - {Feature code} - {Title}`. The surface is Guest app, Partner Hub or Back office, and the feature code comes from the next section. Two titles from the current backlog: `FE - Partner Hub - PHUB - Bulk rate editor` and `BO - Back office - OPS - Refund reason codes`.

## Currencies and locales

Roamstay supports five currencies: `EUR`, `GBP`, `USD`, `CHF` and `SEK`. A partner sets one currency per property in Partner Hub, and the Guest app shows and charges prices in that currency. There is no currency conversion.

Services and events carry money as an integer in minor units. The apps format it for the guest's locale, so the same amount shows as €1,240.50 in `en-GB` and as 1.240,50 € in `de-DE`.

| Locale | Language | Notes |
|--------|----------|-------|
| `en-GB` | English | Default, and the fallback for any missing string |
| `en-US` | English | US spelling, week starts on Sunday |
| `de-DE` | German | Strings run about 30% longer than English, check button widths |
| `fr-FR` | French | Space before the currency sign in prices |
| `es-ES` | Spanish | Space before the currency sign in prices |
| `it-IT` | Italian | Space before the currency sign in prices |
| `nl-NL` | Dutch | Currency sign before the amount, with a space |

Every locale except `en-US` starts the week on Monday. The apps follow the device locale for dates and prices, and the web follows the browser locale. Partner Hub is available in the same seven locales.

## Key flows

### Search

The guest enters a destination, check-in and check-out dates, guests and rooms. A stay runs from 1 night to `30 nights` and check-in can be at most `365 days` ahead. One search covers up to `8 rooms`. `search-service` returns `25 results` per page, sorted by Recommended. The apps load the next page on scroll. The filter sheet holds two filters today, Price and Star rating.

### Property page

The property page shows photos, room types and, for each room type, its rate plans with their cancellation policy and payment option. A partner can set a minimum stay for the property, which the date picker applies on this page.

### Checkout and payment

The guest enters their details and picks a rate plan's payment option. The price breakdown lists the room price per night and the total, with a `City tax` line between them when the property charges it.

With `Pay now`, the payment provider charges the full total, city tax included. The booking waits in `payment_pending` until the payment provider confirms by webhook, then moves to confirmed. A booking still in `payment_pending` after `30 minutes` expires and its room goes back on sale.

With `Pay at property`, the card is stored as a guarantee and the booking confirms at once. The guest pays the property on arrival, city tax included.

### Confirmation and trips

The confirmation screen shows the booking reference, dates, guests and the total. `booking-service` sends the confirmation email at the same moment. The stay then lives under Trips, where the guest can view it, change dates or cancel.

### Cancellation

Before the free cancellation deadline, the guest cancels under Trips and the refund goes back to the card through the payment provider. After the deadline, or on a non-refundable rate plan, the guest contacts Guest Support.

### Partner onboarding today

A partner signs up with a short form on the web. An Ops agent then sets up the property in Back office from the details the partner sends by email. The same agent checks identity and payout details and makes the property live.

## Known constraints

- A stay is at most `30 nights`, and check-in is at most `365 days` ahead
- One booking holds at most `8 rooms`
- A booking in `payment_pending` expires after `30 minutes`
- Prices show and charge in the property's currency, with no conversion
- Roamstay has no loyalty or points scheme. Guests earn no points, and there are no member tiers or member-only prices
- Guests who book with an email address only cannot save a card
- Partner Hub has no mobile app, and its screens are designed for desktop widths
- Back office needs a staff account and is never exposed to partners
- Guest Support covers 07:00 to 23:00 CET, seven days a week

## Analytics conventions

- Event names follow `object_action` in snake_case, with the action in the past tense
- A search filter the guest turns on fires `filter_applied`, with `filter_name` saying which filter
- Every client event carries `app_version`, `session_id`, `platform` and `locale`
- Server events carry the `session_id` of the request that caused them, so client and server events join on it
- Every event carries `source`, which is `client` or `server`
- Money travels as an integer in minor units, in a property whose name ends in `_minor`, with a `currency` property beside it. €129.50 is sent as `12950`
- Events go to `events-collector`, which accepts events from the apps, the web and the services
- The Data team owns the tracking plan. Each event has a row with its trigger, its properties and a status, and a squad builds an event from its row

# Product Owner Hub

One public skill identity over three workflow packets and one transport packet. This hub holds no packet-local logic. It routes by `workflowMode` through `mode-registry.json`, uses `hub-router.json` for router policy, signals and outcomes, and hands stage two to the root `ROUTER.md`, which maps the request's intent to the packet's leaves.

**Version authority.** This file's `version` frontmatter is the hub's release version and matches the newest entry under `changelog/`. `description.json`, `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` carry the same value. `ROUTER.md` keeps its own document version, and each packet keeps its own release line.

Use this skill for Barter backlog and documentation work, for diagrams drawn on FigJam boards, and for the ClickUp and Figma operations those artifacts travel through.

| Mode | Kind | Use it for | Packet |
|------|------|------------|--------|

| **sk-create-figjam** | workflow | A diagram drawn on a FigJam board, from a user flow to a sequence, state, ER or gantt chart: `$flow`, `$figjam` or FigJam output wording with no Product Owner artifact named | [`sk-create-figjam/`](sk-create-figjam/SKILL.md) |
| **mcp-click-up** | workflow | A request that opens with a `cupt` or ClickUp MCP operation, or names one and no Product Owner artifact. Vendored | [`mcp-click-up/`](mcp-click-up/SKILL.md) |

### When NOT to Use

- Editing a vendored packet. A change to `mcp-click-up/` or `mcp-figma/` goes upstream through `scripts/vendor-sync.py push`

## 2. SMART ROUTING

Routing is registry-driven in two stages. Stage one picks the mode here, from `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json`. Stage two is the root [`ROUTER.md`](ROUTER.md), which maps the request's intent to the exact packet-local leaves that mode loads, and the packet's own `SKILL.md` Section 2 routes inside the packet. The hub never emits leaf paths, and `ROUTER.md` never re-decides the mode.

> **Compiled routing (default-on, flag-gated, additive).** Resolve the mode via the compiled router contract first:
> ```bash
> node .skilled/bin/compiled-route.cjs --hub product-owner --prompt "<task>"
> ```
> Follow the returned decision: `route` (use its `targets`), `clarify` or `defer` (disambiguate) or `reject` (refuse). On a `{"servingAuthority":"legacy"}` sentinel or any error, use the routing below. The front door self-gates on serving-authority. Compiled routing is the default for `product-owner`. Set `SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=0`, the explicit kill-switch, to force legacy routing fleet-wide.

`product-owner` ships without a compiled activation manifest, so the directive above returns the legacy sentinel and the stage one rules below route every request. A Product Owner clone that has no `.skilled/bin/` gets an error from the same command and takes the same path.

### Stage One Rules

Stage one follows the ordered rules in [`hub-router.json`](hub-router.json) `routerPolicy.stageOneOrder`. The first matching rule wins. Packet commands run first, then an artifact request, then an opening packet signal, a default artifact word, one non-negated packet signal, and the default mode.

Examples: `cupt list my open tasks` stays in `mcp-click-up` because `tasks` is data, while `figma-ds-cli fj nodes` opens in `mcp-figma`. `figma-ds-cli fj nodes and write a task for the spacing` and `figjam the checkout flow, then write a story` start in `sk-product-owner` because each asks for an artifact. The bare words "figma" and "clickup" remain subjects, and a negated signal such as "do not use figma-ds-cli" starts no packet. A `figma.com/board` link is a FigJam signal, because that address is a FigJam file, while a `figma.com/design` link is not. A full stop ends a clause only before a space, so the dots inside a link stay in the clause that carries it.

A Flow request that stage one keeps in the Product Owner packet follows the single-route handoff contract in [`sk-product-owner/SKILL.md`](sk-product-owner/SKILL.md) Section 2. A command conflict such as `$task $flow` follows that packet's Interactive route.


### Outcomes

- `single`: one packet's commands or signals route to that one mode
- `orderedBundle`: never formed here. Signals of two packets start in the default mode, whose Interactive Mode asks which comes first. A FigJam second output beside an artifact is the exception, because it forms an ordered pair in stage two with the artifact first, while two artifacts still ask
- `defer`: a request with no packet command or signal starts in the default mode, and one it cannot route there gets one clarifying question

`benchmark/hub-routing-cases.json` holds the hub gold rows, and `benchmark/gates/check_hub.py` replays them against these rules and checks that the hub files, the registry, the router and the packets agree.

### Layout

```text

  SKILL.md                 this routing hub
```

`mcp-code-mode/` carries its own `leaf-manifest.json` because it is the Code Mode server this repository ships beside the packets, not a workflow packet, so the rule against a leaf manifest inside a packet does not reach it. Each vendored packet is a byte-identical copy of a shared skill: `vendor.json` records its upstream and `scripts/vendor-sync.py` keeps it in step, so its routing stays in its own `SKILL.md`. Only this hub carries a `graph-metadata.json`, so the advisor discovers one `product-owner` identity.

The packet has one route, Flow Mode, and one choice inside it: the diagram type. This section decides whether a request belongs here and what it loads for that type.

### Primary Detection Signal

```text
$flow | $figjam               -> Flow Mode
FigJam output wording         -> Flow Mode ("make a FigJam flow ...", "a sequence diagram in FigJam")
board notes or a change       -> Flow Mode ("add notes to the FigJam board", "update the FigJam board", any request with a figma.com/board link)
```

A board that already exists is revised here too. Notes go on top through `references/hybrid-workflow.md`, with the target ids from a `get_figjam` read, which works in a session that did not write the board. STYLE_GUIDE = "references/style-guide.md"
```python
HYBRID_WORKFLOW = "references/hybrid-workflow.md"
BOARD_DESIGN = "assets/figjam-design.md"
UNKNOWN_FALLBACK = {

    "needs_disambiguation": True,

    documents = []
    for base in RESOURCE_BASES:
        if base.exists():

    return {path.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for path in documents}

def detect_diagram_types(request):
    text = request.lower()
    return [
        diagram_type for diagram_type, words in TYPE_SIGNALS.items()
        if any(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(word)}(?:s|es)?\b", text) for word in words)
    ]

    if not is_flow_request:
        return UNKNOWN_FALLBACK
    inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
    loaded = []

    def load_if_present(relative_path):
        guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)
        if guarded in inventory and guarded not in loaded:

            loaded.append(guarded)
```

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

Provides the flow-mode workflow for drawing a diagram on a FigJam board. Flow Mode owns the route, the type choice, the intake, the model, the check, the gate, the read-back and the reply. The write composes a framed board from the checked model through one of three routes, and the board is the only deliverable.

### When to Use

Use Flow Mode for any diagram on a FigJam board:
- A user flow drawn from screenshots, Figma frames or a product doc
- A process or decision flow, with a lane per team when work changes hands
- An architecture, a sequence of calls, a state machine, a data model or a dated plan

Use another mode instead for:
- Figma feedback on spacing, copy or alignment, which is a Task
- A written description of a flow or a system, which is a Doc
- A defect seen while walking the flow, which is a Bug

### Command: `$flow`

- **Alias:** `$figjam`. There is no single-letter alias, so `$f` stays free
- **Purpose:** Draw a diagram on a FigJam board
- **Output:** The board URL, one read-back line and the HVR self-scan line, never a file
- **Thinking:** Standard energy, which caps the intake at three rounds, and Deep energy is five. Quick energy is zero rounds: it fills the Brief in Section 4 from the sources and the defaults rather than asking, marks each row it inferred `assumed` with what would settle it and sends one message with the rows, the chosen type and an offer to draw unless corrected. Two failures bracket the intake. Drawing before the rows are covered puts a guessed feature on the board, and asking past a settled row spends a round the reader did not need. The brief that Section 4 sets out is the count, so the threshold and the stop rule can both be read off it.

- No row of the brief is unasked
- The reader and the question are settled
- At most two rows are assumed, and each one names how it gets settled

- The brief is complete and the user confirms it
- Two rounds in a row change no row
- The user says stop
- The energy cap is reached

The cap counts rounds, never questions, because one round is one message however many questions it carries. A later round asks only about a row the sources and the last answers left unasked, such as a gap the answers opened, and never repeats a question. Quick energy is zero rounds, Standard is three and Deep is five. At the cap Flow Mode draws with the assumed rows named, or where the sources cannot carry a diagram it says so and offers a table, as Section 3 sets out. A row still unasked at the cap is named as assumed, never left silent.

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

Provides the flow-mode workflow for drawing a diagram on a FigJam board. Flow Mode owns the route, the type choice, the intake, the model, the check, the gate, the read-back and the reply. The write composes a framed board from the checked model through one of three routes, and the board is the only deliverable.

### When to Use

Use Flow Mode for any diagram on a FigJam board:
- A user flow drawn from screenshots, Figma frames or a product doc
- A process or decision flow, with a lane per team when work changes hands
- An architecture, a sequence of calls, a state machine, a data model or a dated plan

Use another mode instead for:
- Figma feedback on spacing, copy or alignment, which is a Task
- A written description of a flow or a system, which is a Doc
- A defect seen while walking the flow, which is a Bug

### Command: `$flow`

- **Alias:** `$figjam`. There is no single-letter alias, so `$f` stays free
- **Purpose:** Draw a diagram on a FigJam board
- **Output:** The board URL, one read-back line and the HVR self-scan line, never a file
- **Thinking:** Standard energy, which caps the intake at three rounds, and Deep energy is five. Quick energy is zero rounds: it fills the Brief in Section 4 from the sources and the defaults rather than asking, marks each row it inferred `assumed` with what would settle it and sends one message with the rows, the chosen type and an offer to draw unless corrected.
